dashboard.formatDescAdjSwiss: Groups players by their exact, consecutive position in the standings — Table 1 is always the top table with the current leaders. After every round, players move up or down tables based on their new point totals (the style used in TFT lobbies, Commander finals, and poker final tables). Rematches are not avoided when the standings dictate them.
dashboard.formatDescRoundRobin: Mixes tables every round so each player faces new opponents whenever possible. Standings are ignored — everyone keeps playing regardless of results, and repeat pairings are minimized with a search algorithm. Best for casual or social events.
dashboard.formatDescSingleElim: Knockout: only the top half of the standings advances each round; the rest are out. Tables are seeded so the strongest players can't eliminate each other early (1 vs 8, 2 vs 7, ...), and top seeds get byes when the field isn't a perfect bracket size. Best when the event must produce a single champion.
dashboard.formatDescSwiss: Pairs players with similar records: winners face winners and losers face losers, so every round stays competitive. Nobody is eliminated — points accumulate all event. Rematches are avoided when possible without breaking the score groups. Best for competitive events without cuts.

landing.aboutBody1: TableTop Prime is a tournament and league management platform built for board game associations, conventions, and local gaming communities. It handles the operational chaos of running a real-world tournament — pairings, scores, judge calls, standings — so organizers can focus on the game, not the spreadsheet.
landing.aboutBody2: Organizers create an event, add players, and configure scoring rules. The app generates pairings using the Social Golfer algorithm (which guarantees no two players share a table twice), supports Swiss and Round Robin formats, and allows per-round format overrides for phased events. Players submit scores, a second player confirms them, and standings update in real time. Judges receive and acknowledge calls from a live mobile queue.
landing.aboutBody3: Every event can be published to a public share page (at /share/<eventCode>) so parents, friends, and late arrivals can follow standings and current round pairings without an account. Standings and match history can be exported as CSV. Event templates let recurring weekly leagues spin up in seconds.
landing.aboutRoleJudgeDesc: Sees a live queue of player calls, acknowledges and resolves them, edits disputed scores.
landing.aboutRoleOrganizerDesc: Creates the event, adds players, generates pairings, edits scores, dispatches judges, exports CSV.
landing.aboutRolePlayerDesc: Checks in, sees pairings, submits and confirms scores, calls judges, views standings.
landing.badge: New: Adjacent Swiss format for TFT-style finals
landing.feature1Desc: Social Golfer algorithm guarantees no two players share a table twice. Handles drops and late arrivals dynamically.
landing.feature2Desc: Every table score is submitted by one player and confirmed by another — typos and trolling are blocked at the source.
landing.feature3Desc: Players tap "Call Judge" with their table number and issue category. Judges see a live, mobile-optimized queue.
landing.feature4Desc: Transition from Round Robin to Single Elimination with standings carried over automatically.
landing.feature5Desc: Strategy + Decorator pattern lets organizers stack attendance bonuses, round multipliers, and league modifiers.
landing.feature6Desc: Export standings and match history as CSV. Save event templates for recurring weekly leagues with one click.

landing.faqA1: Yes — every player checks in via a QR code or share link on their own phone. There's no app to install; the companion view runs in any modern mobile browser.
landing.faqA2: Yes. The pairing engine handles 2–200+ players across any table size from 2 to 6 per table. Swiss and Adjacent Swiss scale particularly well because they group by standings rather than searching for perfect pairings.
landing.faqA3: Yes. Standings and full match history (every table, every round, every placement) can be exported as CSV at any time. Great for league records and end-of-season reports.
landing.faqA4: Yes — the Free tier supports up to 11 players with all pairing formats, dual-score verification, and live standings. Paid tiers unlock larger events, judge dispatch, CSV export, and event templates. See the pricing section below.
landing.faqA5: No. Players open a share link in their browser, enter their name, and they're in. Organizers can also add players manually from the dashboard if they don't have a phone.
landing.faqA6: Every table score is submitted by one player and must be confirmed by a second player at the same table before it's locked. This catches typos, misclicks, and bad-faith submissions at the source. Judges can also edit disputed scores after the fact.
